brand.title: ESourceAIG (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — ESource Team: How to Activate a New Accounting Firm

questions.question: What is the web address of the admin page where you add a new firm?
questions.feedback_correct: That's right—app.esourcebookkeeper.com/admin.html is where you open the admin page with the admin key.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The admin page is found at app.esourcebookkeeper.com/admin.html. This is the central place where you manage firm activation and billing.

questions.question: How much does the first client book cost under the standard pricing plan?
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—the first book costs twenty dollars, then the rates drop for books in higher bands.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The first book is twenty dollars. Books two through ten are seventeen dollars, books eleven through thirty are fifteen dollars, and so on.

questions.question: What must you choose carefully in Step 1 because it never changes?
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—the Firm ID is short, lowercase with no spaces, and once chosen it cannot be changed.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The Firm ID is the unique identifier you pick in Step 1 (like smithco) and it's permanent, so it must be chosen with care. Other settings like logo and limits can be adjusted later.

questions.question: In Step 3, what should the proxy cloud setting be in Cloudflare?
questions.feedback_correct: That's correct—set the proxy cloud to gray (DNS only); an orange cloud would block Vercel's security certificate.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The proxy cloud must be set to gray, which means DNS only. An orange cloud blocks Vercel's security certificate and prevents the domain from working properly.

questions.question: What is the name of the AI assistant mentioned in the course that answers how-to questions for firms?
questions.feedback_correct: Right—Bill is the help assistant, and his assistant ID can be kept in the firm's profile to provide the Ask Bill button.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The help assistant is named Bill. You can keep ESource's assistant ID in the firm's profile settings to give them access to Bill, or leave it blank to hide the Ask Bill button.

questions.question: How often should you check the License Service to bill each firm for their client books?
choices: Whenever a client is added or removed
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—you open the admin page once a month and click Load firms to read each firm's highest book count for billing.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Billing happens monthly. You load the firms from the admin page once per month and bill based on the 'Highest by month' number, which tracks the peak client book count on any single day that month.

questions.question: What must be true before you activate a new firm, according to the "Before you activate" slide?
choices: The firm must have at least one staff member already hired
The firm's web address must already be live
The white-label license agreement must be signed by both sides
The first client must already be imported into the system
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—the signed license agreement is the first of four things that must be in place before activation begins.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The white-label license agreement must be signed by both sides before you activate. The other three requirements are the agreed plan and tier, a quote confirming the client book limit, and the owner's details. Staff and clients come later.

questions.question: If a computer goes without internet for fourteen days, what happens to its access to the firm's books?
choices: The user receives a warning but can continue working
The computer automatically syncs and catches up when reconnected
The computer locks for safety until the user connects and signs in again
The firm's owner must manually unlock the computer on the admin page
questions.feedback_correct: That's right—a fourteen-day internet outage triggers a lock for safety, and the user must reconnect and sign in to restore access.
questions.feedback_incorrect: For security, any computer offline for fourteen days is locked automatically. The user just needs to reconnect to the internet and sign in again to regain access to the books.

questions.question: When billing a firm with the highest book count of 15 clients in a month, which price bands apply?
choices: Twenty dollars for book 1, seventeen dollars for books 2–10, and fifteen dollars for books 11–15
Twenty dollars for book 1 and fifteen dollars for books 2–15
Twenty dollars for book 1, seventeen dollars for books 2–10, and fourteen dollars for books 11–15
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—you apply each rate only to books in its band: the first book is twenty dollars, books two through ten are seventeen dollars each, and books eleven through thirty are fifteen dollars each.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The band pricing is specific: $20 for book 1, $17 for books 2–10, $15 for books 11–30, $14 for books 31–100, and $13 after that. Each band's rate applies only to the books in that range, so a firm with 15 books pays all three rates.

questions.question: According to the course, what should you do when a firm asks about how its data is handled or about other accounting software?
choices: Provide detailed explanations about ESource's data storage and promise the firm will own their data
Refer them to the data security section in the user guide they receive
Speak only about ESource and bring in the product owner for other questions
Explain that ESource uses standard cloud encryption like all modern software
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—when firms ask about data or other software, you should speak only about ESource and bring the product owner into the conversation.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course emphasizes that you should speak only about ESource when discussing data handling or other software. If the firm has questions beyond that, involve the product owner rather than making promises on your own.
